title: Geometric reducedness detected by a chosen algebraic closure
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension], let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and fix an algebraic closure $\bar k/k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Then $X$ is geometrically reduced over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], meaning that $X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ is reduced for every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-reduced-scheme], if and only if $X_{\bar k}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ is reduced. No finite-type, quasi-compactness, or nonemptiness hypothesis on $X$ is imposed; the empty scheme is included.

source.place: Tag 035X (lemma-geometrically-reduced), equivalence (2) iff (6) in characteristic p > 0; Tag 020I (lemma-perfect-reduced) in characteristic zero, together with descent of reducedness along the faithfully flat field extension k to its algebraic closure.

proof.text: Geometric reducedness applied to the extension Ω/k gives reducedness of X_Ω directly, using the chosen pullback square. This direction needs no finiteness or nonemptiness assumption.

Assume X_Ω is reduced. IsAlgClosure.isAlgClosed makes Ω algebraically closed and hence perfect. Apply the existing, fully proved library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyReduced.of_perfectField to X_Ω → Spec Ω. That theorem proves geometric reducedness by an affine open cover, pullbackSpecIso, reducedness of tensor products over a perfect field, affine_isReduced_iff, and IsReduced.of_openCover. Its statement has no finite-type hypothesis.

Fix any extension K/k and put M = AlgebraicClosure K, in the same universe. Since Ω/k is algebraic and M is algebraically closed, IsAlgClosed.lift supplies a k-algebra map Ω → M; use its induced Ω-algebra structure and scalar-tower identity. Geometric reducedness of X_Ω gives reducedness of X_Ω ×_Ω Spec M. Pullback pasting identifies this with X_K ×_K Spec M: the two composites Spec M → Spec k coincide by the scalar-tower equations. The comparison is explicitly the composite of two pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso isomorphisms and pullback.congrHom. Thus the latter scheme is reduced.

The map g:Spec M → Spec K is surjective, since both spectra are nonempty singletons. Its target is reduced, so IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.of_isDominant makes g scheme-theoretically dominant. It is quasi-compact because it is a morphism of affine schemes. The map X_K → Spec K is flat by the field-flatness lemma. Flat base change therefore makes q:X_K ×_K Spec M → X_K quasi-compact and scheme-theoretically dominant.

Apply Mathlib IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.isReduced to q. Explicitly, quasi-compact schematic dominance makes each map on sections injective, and the source section rings are reduced; hence the target section rings are reduced as well. Thus X_K is reduced. The criterion geometrically_iff_of_commRing_of_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms packages this for every K/k into GeometricallyReduced of the original structure map. No point of X is chosen, so this includes X empty.

proof_origin.place: Tag 020I (perfect reduced schemes), with common algebraically closed overfield and schematic-dominance descent (morphisms.tex Tags 081I and 056B); reuses the complete source theorem GeometricallyReduced.of_perfectField.
